note: Second pass today: rebuilt from fresh Sleeper rosters/trending and confirmed no Week 2 waiver moves league-wide yet. 18 verified-unrostered targets off the top of the trending-add list and this week's news pass; Devaughn Vele stays off the board (bwalsh89's roster). Two claims planned, 20 dollars committed if both hit, 80 left.

targets.hook: 84% snaps, 9 targets, 8-138-2; ankle boot is precautionary
targets.why: Played 57 of 68 snaps and turned 9 targets into 8-138-2 (29.8 pts here) in Carolina's 59-37 shootout loss to Chicago. Rolled his ankle in the first quarter, finished the game, and was seen in a walking boot Monday that he called precautionary, saying he expects to play Week 2 vs. Atlanta (NBC Sports, DraftSharks, heavy.com, Sept. 14-15).
targets.asset: 84% snap share and 9 targets in a shootout; Sleeper projects 10.2 for Week 2, the highest of any unrostered WR here
targets.my_team_impact: Cracks the lineup: his 10.2 projection beats Tuten (8.2) at FLEX and Egbuka (9.1) at WR2. Replaces Boutte, who ran 36 of 79 snaps for 2 targets.
targets.confidence_why: One game, and a real ankle to monitor through Wednesday's practice report; the role is big but unproven past Week 1.
targets.competition: Three WR-needy rivals with a full 100: pauldag (A.J. Brown IR six weeks, Flowers out; price_to_beat 18, n_contested 35), Sladsous (Thomas and Pierce questionable; 27) and bwalsh89 (McConkey day-to-day, Tyson IR; 28).
targets.bid: 15 dollars -- above the contested-routine band (8-12) and well past pauldag's median bid (2.5), but short of his p90 18 and far short of Sladsous/bwalsh89 if they chase. Don't go past 15 on one game.
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte -- 36 of 79 snaps, 2 targets, 2.6 pts; not scoopable in any way that matters.

targets.hook: Rookie at 86% route share, 7 targets, 5-94 in debut
targets.why: Third-round rookie started, ran a route on 86 percent of Willis's dropbacks, and turned a 26 percent target share into 5 catches for 94 yards (RotoWire, Yahoo Sports, Sept. 14-15); dolphinseer.com flagged him outperforming Jaylen Waddle in the opener. Sleeper's #2 trending add league-wide.
targets.asset: 86% route share, 7 targets, 13.4 yards per target; projects 7.0 for Week 2
targets.my_team_impact: Bench piece now, not a starter (7.0 trails Tuten's 8.2). A WR with a full-time role beats a zero-touch handcuff while Jeanty is healthy, and he's the next man up if Egbuka or Pickens miss.
targets.confidence_why: Full-time snaps are a sturdier signal than one big stat line, but it's still one game from a rookie on a run-first offense.
targets.competition: Same three WR-needy rivals as Coker. Most of the trending volume is other leagues; FantasyPros prices him at 2% true value.
targets.bid: 5 dollars -- clears the routine-uncontested band (1-3). If he goes higher, pivot to Malik Washington (same offense, 8 targets) rather than chasing.
targets.drop: Mike Washington -- 13 of 68 snaps behind a healthy Jeanty; only worth holding as a handcuff, and 3.5 projected points isn't that.

targets.hook: Route parity with DeVonta Smith; 73 yds, TD on 4 targets
targets.why: Ran nearly identical snap and route counts to DeVonta Smith in Week 1 (50 of 55 snaps), catching a 64-yarder and a 9-yard touchdown on just 4 targets (FantasyPros, Sept. 15).
targets.asset: 91% snap share, but only 4 targets; projects 6.8
targets.my_team_impact: Not a starter at 6.8. Only relevant if Coker's price runs away and you still want to replace Boutte.
targets.confidence_why: The routes are real, but 14.3 of his points came from two splash plays on four looks.
targets.competition: Sladsous owns DeVonta Smith and is WR-needy, a correlated add for that roster.
targets.bid: n/a -- watch; a 1-3 dollar fallback claim if both PURSUEs miss
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte, only if Coker isn't claimed.

targets.hook: A.J. Brown out six weeks; 22 second-half routes
targets.why: A.J. Brown landed on IR with a high-ankle sprain now expected to cost six weeks, not four (Rapoport via NFL.com, Sept. 14). Hollins ran 4 routes in the first half and 22 in the second after Brown went down, catching 4 of 5 for a team-high 51 yards (Fantasy Footballers, Sept. 14).
targets.asset: 50 of 71 snaps with most of it after the injury; projects 7.1
targets.my_team_impact: Bench depth with a real six-week window. Doesn't beat Tuten or Egbuka.
targets.confidence_why: Half a game of role, and Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas compete for the same vacated targets.
targets.competition: mfkr owns Doubs; pauldag owns Brown and has the most obvious reason to bid on his replacement.
targets.bid: n/a -- watch; see who actually wins the Brown targets in Week 2
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte, if you pivot here.

targets.hook: 55 of 56 snaps and 8 targets, the pivot if Douglas runs
targets.why: Played 55 of 56 snaps with a team-high 8 targets (3-53) in Week 1, per Sleeper's stat line. Same Miami offense and a near-identical projection to Caleb Douglas, with a quarter of the attention (trending #57 against Douglas's #2).
targets.asset: 98% snap share, 8 targets, an inefficient 3 catches; projects 7.1
targets.my_team_impact: Same bench slot as Douglas; don't claim both.
targets.confidence_why: Volume without production in one game; Douglas's efficiency is why he leads.
targets.competition: Nobody's roster points at him specifically; WR-needy rivals will look at Douglas first.
targets.bid: n/a -- watch; the 1-3 dollar backup if Douglas clears past 5

targets.hook: Flowers and Lane both hurt; 78% snaps but 1 target
targets.why: Zay Flowers (hamstring, day-to-day, 'not considered serious' per Rapoport) and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (fractured wrist, expected weeks) both left Baltimore's win over Indianapolis; Bateman reclaims boundary duties (RotoWire, NBC Sports, Sept. 14).
targets.asset: 53 of 68 snaps for 1 target and 0 points; projects 7.2
targets.rate_basis: projection (opportunity-driven; wk 1 usage didn't show it)
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't start for you, and 1 target on 53 snaps is exactly the profile Boutte already has.
targets.confidence_why: The opportunity is an injury report, not a demonstrated role yet.
targets.competition: pauldag owns Flowers, a correlated hedge (price_to_beat 18).
targets.bid: n/a -- watch through the Ravens' Wednesday practice report

targets.hook: Projects 20.8, above Herbert, but you only start one QB
targets.why: mfkr dropped him in Week 1 for Malik Davis. Went for 205 yards and 3 TDs plus 29 rushing yards (22.1 pts) in a win over the Rams, and Sleeper projects 20.8 for Week 2.
targets.asset: Full-time starter, 22.1 pts in Week 1; 20.8 projected
targets.my_team_impact: Outprojects Herbert (16.9) this week, but a 5-man bench can't carry a QB2 in a one-QB, 10-team league where a streamer exists every week. Revisit for Herbert's bye.
targets.confidence_why: Structural: one QB slot and a short bench, not a read on Purdy himself.
targets.competition: DiaperDutyDaddy has Kyler Murray in concussion protocol (price_to_beat 21, n_contested 50) and is the natural bidder.

targets.hook: 32.4 pts in Week 1 shootout; no QB slot for him
targets.why: Threw for 361 yards and 3 TDs with a rushing score (32.4 pts here) in the 59-37 loss to Chicago; 9.8 yards per attempt (FantasyPros, Sept. 15). Projects 16.0 for Week 2.
targets.asset: One huge game in a shootout; 16.0 projected
targets.my_team_impact: No fit. Herbert starts, and Young projects below him.
targets.confidence_why: Structural, and his own projection agrees.
targets.competition: DiaperDutyDaddy is the QB-needy team (Murray in protocol).

targets.hook: Starts at Chicago if Murray doesn't clear the protocol
targets.why: Relieved Kyler Murray (concussion protocol) for 3 touchdowns in Week 1; Murray told the team he 'feels pretty good' Monday but Kevin O'Connell says his Week 2 status is day-by-day and far from decided, with Wentz the presumptive starter if he sits (Star Tribune, valleynewslive.com, Sept. 15).
targets.asset: 19.2 pts in relief; a one-week streamer at most
targets.confidence_why: Nothing about your roster depends on this news.
targets.competition: DiaperDutyDaddy owns Murray and is the rival actually exposed.

targets.hook: 8 targets, faces the league's worst TE defense of 2025
targets.why: Drew 8 targets (4-35) in Week 1, and Week 2 draws Cincinnati, which allowed a league-high 116 catches and 16 TDs to tight ends last season (FantasyPros, Sept. 15). Projects 7.9.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't beat LaPorta, and a hair below Ferguson's 8.2 as the backup. A streaming option for LaPorta's bye, not now.
targets.confidence_why: Two tight ends already, both projecting at or above him.
targets.competition: bwalsh89 has Brock Bowers out (meniscus) and is the TE-needy team (price_to_beat 28).

targets.hook: 11.8 pts on 10 touches in a three-way committee
targets.why: Scored 11.8 on 6 carries and 4 targets over 25 of 69 snaps, Sleeper's stat line. Still listed behind Cam Skattebo in a Giants backfield that also holds Tyrone Tracy and Najee Harris (CBS Sports). Sleeper's #3 trending add league-wide, on the strength of the box score.
targets.my_team_impact: No path: five RBs already on your roster, and he projects under Mike Washington's floor role.
targets.confidence_why: A 3.2 projection says the market is chasing one box score.
targets.competition: DadKing (Henderson out, Charbonnet limited) and DiaperDutyDaddy (Kamara out) are RB-needy and may bite.

targets.hook: 23.8 pts on 8 targets, but only 49% of snaps
targets.why: Caught 8 of 8 targets for 78 yards and 2 TDs (23.8 pts) on 34 of 69 snaps, per Sleeper's stat line. Projects 7.4 for Week 2.
targets.asset: Part-time snaps, full-time production for one week; 7.4 projected
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't beat LaPorta or Ferguson on projection.
targets.confidence_why: Two touchdowns on half the snaps is the least repeatable line on the wire.
targets.competition: bwalsh89 (Bowers out) is the TE-needy bidder.

targets.hook: Led Bengals in targets on just 33% of snaps
targets.why: Led Cincinnati in catches, targets and yards with 5-78-1 on 7 targets in the win over Tampa Bay (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Sept. 13), on only 21 of 64 snaps.
targets.my_team_impact: No fit behind LaPorta and Ferguson.
targets.confidence_why: A one-third snap share with Chase and Higgins healthy won't hold seven targets for long.
targets.competition: bwalsh89 is the only TE-needy roster.

targets.hook: Tied for team lead in targets in a run-heavy offense
targets.why: Tied for Pittsburgh's team lead in targets and accounted for nearly a quarter of Aaron Rodgers' passing yards despite a run-heavy script (RotoWire, Sept. 14). 5-46-1 on 49 of 67 snaps.
targets.my_team_impact: Below both of your tight ends on projection.
targets.confidence_why: Roster fit, not a knock on the role.

targets.hook: Next up behind Judkins with Sampson out extended time
targets.why: Dylan Sampson left Cleveland's loss at Jacksonville on crutches with a knee injury now expected to cost extended time, not just Week 2; Sanders is next behind Quinshon Judkins (nfl-events feed, Sept. 14). Week 1: 1 carry, 3 targets on 18 of 51 snaps.
targets.asset: Change-of-pace role that just grew; projects 5.1
targets.my_team_impact: A handcuff to someone else's back; no use to your RB room.
targets.confidence_why: No correlation to your roster and no standalone role yet.
targets.competition: Stipe owns Judkins (price_to_beat 23) and is the natural handcuff bidder; DadKing is RB-needy.

targets.hook: Out-carried McCaffrey 14-10 in a deliberate split
targets.why: Rookie played 28 snaps to McCaffrey's 35 and out-carried him 14-10 with identical 15 total touches; Shanahan called the split deliberate (nfl-events feed, Sept. 14). FantasyPros prices him at 9% true value, 17% for a desperate team (Sept. 15).
targets.my_team_impact: Would be your sixth RB and doesn't beat Tuten (8.2). Not your handcuff: Sladsous owns McCaffrey.
targets.confidence_why: The committee is real; the verdict rests on the price three RB-needy rivals will pay for it.
targets.competition: Sladsous (price_to_beat 27) for the handcuff, DadKing (16) and DiaperDutyDaddy (21) for the carries.
targets.bid: n/a -- pass; the clearing price will be well above what a sixth RB is worth to you

targets.hook: 3 targets and a long TD; yesterday's top add, now outranked
targets.why: Named San Francisco's WR3 with Christian Kirk (IR) and Ricky Pearsall out, then scored on a 39-yard catch in a 2-catch, 3-target Week 1 (NBC Sports, Sept. 10).
targets.my_team_impact: Coker and Douglas both project higher for the same bench slot.
targets.confidence_why: Downgraded on relative value once Week 1 usage for the whole wire was in, not on new news about him.
targets.competition: No WR-needy rival has a reason to prefer him over the names above.

targets.hook: 9 targets in Week 1, taken largely from Odunze's share
targets.why: Caught 8 of 9 targets for 84 yards against Carolina, nearly double the next Bear (Luther Burden, 5), while running a route on 23 of 40 Caleb Williams dropbacks (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Sept. 13).
targets.my_team_impact: Not an add, but a flag on your own bench: Odunze drew only 3 targets on 36 of 75 snaps coming off his calf in the same game. If Raymond's share holds in Week 2, Odunze is your next drop, not a FLEX option.
targets.confidence_why: A 4.5 projection says Sleeper reads the target spike as game-specific.
targets.competition: pauldag owns Burden and is WR-needy, but has better options above.
